title: Introduction to if statements
recap: An if statement executes its following statement only when its condition converts to true. An if-else chain selects the first true branch and skips the remaining branches.
Ordering and matching conditions matter. A three-way comparison can handle positive, negative, and zero values with if, else if, and a final else.
objectives: Write mutually exclusive branches with an if-else chain.
Match negative, positive, and zero values to the correct output.
Recognize that the final else handles the remaining case.
Exercise every branch with deterministic calls.
warnings: Only the first true branch in an if-else chain executes.
A condition and its printed label must describe the same case.
Do not replace the fixed calls with three hard-coded report lines.
challenge: Repair printTemperatureState() so negative temperatures print below freezing, positive temperatures print above freezing, and zero prints freezing point. Use one if/else-if/else chain and keep all three supplied calls so every path executes in a deterministic no-input run.
hints: The first condition should identify values less than zero.
After the negative case, test values greater than zero.
If neither comparison is true, the value must be zero.
